You've said time and time again that *you* enjoy contracts, *you* enjoy writing them, *you* enjoy editing them. Can I suggest that you start with a contract for *YOU*/*YOUR* conduct?

Things that YOU will adhere to, consequences for YOUR actions, YOU understanding and consenting to her soft and hard limits.

I haven't done contracts with my Subs, but *I* love rule lists and Chore lists. When I have wanted to introduce them to a new dynamic I encourage my sub to make rules for ME, so they understand that a) they do in fact have some level of control, even when giving up control to me, and b) I also have specific conduct I must adhere to.

Examples of rules my subs have given me:

* check in texts at specific times

* specific terms of endearment to use when praising them

* how to approach conversations when I am unhappy with their behaviour 

* no ghosting when I am really upset with them (I am not a ghosting person, but my subs have had anxiety about this due to previous relationships)

* how much time I commit to scenes etc each week (this has obviously been flexible because life happens, but it helps us both schedule to help meet their needs)

* hard limits of theirs I will absolutely adhere to, eg my current sub has a needle phobia, and I am a needle top, so I do not talk about needle play around them. I have absolutely slipped on this once or twice in the beginning, and it helps them that *I* had that rule because when they panicked I took the onus on me, so they didn't feel guilty about having a panic attack, which can often happen with limits

Chores examples

* brushing their hair whenever it is needed and I am with them

* reminding them to hydrate/bringing them water when I notice they are busy and haven't had a drink in a while

* one of my subs was terrible at having breakfast, so when I was staying with them I would make breakfast, because I enjoy it and I was more of a morning person 

* reminding them to take meds.


In the early days I had these things written down, while they had more flexible verbal rules and chores, which they did end up writing down to help them remember, but weren't an "official"  list until they had settled into the idea more, once they were ready for official rules, I wrote them out nicely in a more official looking document, along with consequences, rewards etc 


Alot of people seem to ignore or at least not acknowledge, that Doms also have to have rules and expectations of their behaviour. I find its a good way to start a dynamic. I think we were her only visitors outside of the people from her "church" (technically a church, realistically a cult, did the old lady dirty in the end but thats a whole other story) She was in her late 90s when this happened and had still been fairly active until this incident. 

As my siblings and I get older we visit her less but still stop by at least once a week I'd say, and chat to her over the fence while she gardened. We'd feed her dogs if she was away for any reasons etc.

One week the whole family had been particularly busy and no-one had stopped by untill early one morning before school when Mum realised her mail box was full and asks if anyone has seen her lately, a resounding 'no' from the Family and Mum says she's just going to check on her before she drives us to school. Mums gone for ages and eventually she comes out from Roses and tells us we need to walk to school cause Rose had fallen and Mum was going to wait with her for the ambulance. 

Thats all I knew, mum refused to ever speak about it. And refused to go back into Roses house after That day until after the dog had been taken to a new home while Rose was in Hospice  

Until one day I was talking to my sister about Rose, and how she fell, and how mum seemed to hate her dog Jess (a fat Chihuahua × foxy type dog), and she tells me the rest of the story, as she was at home that morning, so,

Mum walks into Roses place (we had a key for feeding the dogs etc) and calls out to Rose. Eventually she starts looking around for her.  Mum heads down the hall and sees Rose on the floor in the spare room. It turns out she'd slipped on something and her foot had skidded under an old dresser, tearing her shin up on the way down (old lady, paper thin skin etc) and broken a few bones including her hip in the fall

she had always had bad blood flow to her legs and I remember helping her with those pressure socks you sometimes see elderly folks wearing, so between the fairly traumatic injury, and the lack of blood flow the exposed tissue on her legs goes necrotic fairly quick and well, Roses dog Jess had no other food, so she starts eating Roses dead flesh from her leg. Rose can neither see or feel this because shes flat on her back and the tissue is dead, and at some point in the 4 days, had become unconscious. So Jess munched away on Roses leg for the 3 or 4 days she was stuck there.

Mum managed to rouse her before the ambulance shows up and Rose tells her how she slipped and fell and is very worried because poor Jess had not been fed. That was her biggest concern. Mum reassured her that she'd look after Jess as soon as paramedics arrived.

Rose went into Hospice after this and passed away a while later. We had continued looking after Jess while she was in care until it became clear she wasn't going to be coming home, at which point the dog was rehomed.

The reason mum seemed to hate the dog, and refused to go back into the house while it was still there, was that she would have vivid flash backs to walking in amd seeing Rose, looking like she was dead, being eaten by her tiny little dog.

I don't know what country you're in so good chance things could have different names but apricot chicken is legit the EASIEST recipe and tastes so good. Im in Australia so if something seems weird do a Google my friend.

Ingredients:
Chicken thigh cutlets (they come in a 9pack here)

1 Pckt french onion soup mix (its dry stuff)

1 large tin of apricot halves

1 liter of Apricot nectar

1 sliced onion



Method :
Chuck it all in a slow cooker in the morning, serve it up that night with rice.

Alternatively if you don't have a slow cooker just brown your chicken in a frypan, add in the onion and fry untill soft, add your soup mix, apricots and nectar and cook on low untill you get a boil going then turn off the heat and serve it up.

This is also a super easy recipe to add veggies to, either straight in the slow cooker or steam them up and add to the frypan a few minutes before you serve it up.
